memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'During the entire period of their Nazirite vow, no razor may be used on their head. They must be holy until the period of their dedication to the Lord is over; they must let their hair grow long.' - Num 6:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The most visible sign of a Nazirite was uncut hair. Throughout the period of the vow, no razor touched their head. Anyone who saw them would know at a glance: this person has set themselves apart for God. Their devotion was not hidden; it was worn openly.

There is a lesson here about a faith that can be seen. The Nazirite's commitment was not merely a private feeling in the heart; it showed in a way others could recognise. True devotion to God, while it begins in the heart, naturally becomes visible in a life.

Jesus said that His followers are the light of the world, and that our light should shine before others so that they see our good works and glorify God (Matt 5:14-16). We are not called to hide our faith in embarrassment, but to live it openly, so that God is honoured.

At the same time, the point was never showing off. The Nazirite's long hair was not about drawing attention to himself, but about pointing to his dedication to God. There is a world of difference between living faith openly for God's glory and parading our religion for our own.

Is your faith visible in how you live? Not loud or showy, but genuine — the kind of life that quietly makes people think of God. Let your devotion show, for His glory and not your own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is your faith visible in the way you live?
- Do you ever hide your faith out of embarrassment?
- How can you live openly for God's glory rather than your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let my devotion to You be seen in how I live — not to draw attention to myself, but to point others to You. Amen.
